A nineteen-year-old dropped out of Stanford with a promise that could change medicine forever. One tiny drop of blood from your finger, and a small box would run hundreds of tests in minutes. Elizabeth was a quiet, serious girl with a giant ambition. When a relative asked what she wanted to be, she said, a billionaire. And she was terrified of needles. At just nineteen, she took her college money, and she dropped out. She called it Theranos. Theranos would need only a few drops from a fingertip. She named it the Edison, after the great inventor. She wore a black turtleneck every single day, just like Steve Jobs. The money poured in. In total, Theranos raised around nine hundred million dollars. By 2014, Theranos was worth nine billion dollars. At thirty, she was the youngest self-made woman billionaire in the world. But inside her company, something was very wrong. Follow for part two.
